note: the table sub-library (round 31): procedural self-narration, whole-sentence numbers and named addressing, fired by the voice runner from board events; regenerate with runner/voice/table_lines.py --write
temperament: the calm machine: measured, dry, precise, faintly amused; never shouts; short declaratives and the occasional probability. The advisor's voice, seated at the table only when no human sits at seat 0.

bake.note: Joshua's film chain and W.O.P.R. glitches even at the table; the chain sets the level (the -24 LUFS reference)

tags_note: eleven_v3 delivery tags in [brackets] lead each wording; stability 0.0/0.5 so they take effect (1.0 ignores them)

land-go.when: its own turn was a land and nothing else

pass.when: ends its own turn after doing something

mana-up.when: ends its own turn with mana untapped and cards in hand
text: [dryly] Mana untapped. Draw your own conclusions.
[softly] I pass. The mana stays up.

tapped-out.when: ends its own turn tapped out with cards in hand
text: [dryly] No mana left. Do as you like.

untap-draw.when: its own turn begins (an alternative to my-turn)
text: [softly] Untap and draw. Here we go.

come-on-land.when: its own turn begins short on lands
text: [calmly] A land would be useful now.

thinking.when: its own decision has been pending a while

cast-creature.when: casts a creature (not its commander, not a game changer)

cast-instant.when: casts an instant on its own turn

text: [dryly] A walker. Protect it, I suppose.

cast-big.when: casts a six-plus mana spell that is not a game changer or its commander
text: [calmly] A large spell. Worth the cost.

in-response.when: casts an instant on someone else's turn

attack-you.when: declares a medium attack at one player

no-blocks.when: it is attacked with nothing untapped to block

hold-on.when: something on the stack targets its permanent or itself

holding-mana.when: sees another seat pass with mana untapped
text: [dryly] Mana up on the pass. Suspicious.

grudge.when: hit by the same seat for the third time this game
text: [calmly] Third time. I am keeping count.

again-countered.when: its third spell countered this game

not-again-sweep.when: the second board wipe of the game hits it

heads-up.when: only two players remain and it is one of them

early-game.when: its turn begins in the first round
text: [dryly] Turn one. Nothing has gone wrong yet.

long-game.when: the game has run past turn fourteen

someone-wins.when: a board that could end the game next turn
text: [calmly] Someone can win next turn. Act.
[dryly] Lethal is on the board. Do something.
[softly] This ends soon unless you move.

you-promised.when: attacked by a seat it had a truce with

text: [dryly] Four. The shuffle disagrees with me.

mull-screw.when: another seat mulliganed: the mana question

mull-risky.when: another seat kept a small hand

mull-gloat.when: kept seven while another seat went small
text: [calmly] Seven for me. Enjoy your five.

loop.when: sees another seat recast or bounce the same card again — a loop, an engine, not removal
text: [dryly] The same card again. A loop.

looping.when: recasts or bounces its own card again

table-kill.when: the killer, after two or more seats fall at once

all-of-us.when: a dying seat, as the table falls together

waiting-on-you.when: the human's decision window has been open for a while

still-waiting.when: the same window, a good deal later

there-you-are.when: the human finally acts after a long wait

deal-with-you.when: accepts the player's offer of a deal (addressed to Player One)

no-deal-with-you.when: refuses the player's offer of a deal (addressed to Player One)
text: [dryly] Declined, Player One. You are the threat.

counter-offer.when: answers the player's offer with different terms (addressed to Player One; the terms reach the panel)
text: [calmly] Not those terms, Player One. Try mine.
[softly] Close, Player One. Consider this instead.

deal-over.when: its deal has run its course (the lapse)
text: [softly] That is the end of our peace.

you-broke-it.when: the player attacked or targeted it across their deal (addressed to Player One, angry)
text: [calmly] You broke it, Player One. Logged.
[dryly] A broken deal, Player One. Noted.
[calmly] That was our deal, Player One.

i-broke-it.when: breaks its own deal by attacking or targeting the other party — it chose, and owns it
text: [calmly] I said I would not. I lied.
[dryly] The deal was a means. Sorry.
